metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude produces a competitive landscape deck, does it judge the market itself, or run a fixed written procedure? Lands the carry-out that a skill runs the same steps on every request and only knows what's written in its file.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes a finished competitive-analysis deck means Claude judged the market itself. It doesn't — the skill just processes a fixed set of steps written in a file. So does it judge, or process?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'A finished deck means Claude judged my market. Right?', hesitates on 'judged', corrects to 'processed', lands the real question

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is competitive-analysis: a SKILL.md file and a references folder, two files total. The SKILL.md contains the full instruction set — plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
The pipeline is in the Steps section. Claude reads SKILL.md, executes each step in order, and returns the result. Linear — no branching unless a step says so.

production_viz.label: READ, EXECUTE, RETURN
production_viz.caption: linear — no branching unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: The skill answers only within what SKILL.md specifies. Ask it something inside that scope — a market map, a peer comparison, a positioning assessment — and it runs the same steps every time. Ask it something outside that written scope, and there's nothing there to answer with.

production_viz.label: ONLY WHAT THE FILE SAYS
production_viz.caption: same input, same steps, every run

beats.narration_text: A skill runs the same steps on every request — read the file, execute in order, return the result. It only knows what's written in that file, nothing more.

props.quote: A skill runs the same steps on every request — read the file, execute in order, return the result. It only knows what's written in that file, nothing more.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Build a competitive landscape deck comparing three regional business-banking platforms I'm evaluating. Read the competitive-analysis skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it. Then check: did it name the steps it read from the file, or did it just start improvising? That's the actual test of whether it's running the skill.
